label: conj:two-filtration-bridge
title: Two-filtration bridge: iterated-integral depth $\leftrightarrow$ partition-cellular GB-depth via $e_\lambda$
html:
The substrate convolution Hopf algebra \mathcal{H}_q carries two distinct filtrations:

  • the iterated-integral depth on grouplikes, G^{(0)} \subseteq G^{(1)} \subseteq \cdots with G^{(n)} generated by \{\exp_q, \log_q, \mathrm{Li}_2^q, \ldots, \mathrm{Li}_n^q\};
  • the partition max-hook filtration on the centre Z(H_n(q)), Z^{(0)}(A) \subseteq Z^{(1)}(A) \subseteq \cdots generated by the central idempotents e_\lambda with \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda) := \max_{\square \in \lambda} h(\square) (a partition-level filtration distinct from the word-level curvature-rank filtration of curvature-rank GB stratification used in stratified \Phi_q; identifying word rewrite depth with partition hook length remains unestablished).

Terminology. The statistic \max_\square h(\square) = \lambda_1+\lambda'_1-1 used in this block is now called the max-hook depth. The corpus fixes "GB-depth" to mean Lusztig's a-function a(\lambda)=\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}{2}; see Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)), which also shows that either choice gives a filtration of Z(H_n(q)) by ideals, not a unital algebra filtration. Below, \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}} should be read as the max-hook depth.

These are different numbers — for the figure-8 self-conjugate cell \lambda = (2, 2), iterated-integral depth = 2 but partition GB-depth = 3 (max hook length). The conjecture: they are related, and the bridge is via the central primitive idempotents e_\lambda.

Statement

For each \lambda \vdash n, the central idempotent e_\lambda \in Z(H_n(q)) has a canonical iterated-integral depth lift \hat{e}_\lambda \in G^{(d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda))}(\mathcal{H}_q) where the depth d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) is given by:

  d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    2 & \text{if } \lambda \text{ is self-conjugate (amphichiral cell)} \\
    3 & \text{if } \lambda, \lambda' \text{ form a chiral pair} \\
    \min(\mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}}(\lambda), 2\,\lceil n/2 \rceil) & \text{otherwise}
  \end{cases}

The third branch is empty: every partition is either self-conjugate or one half of the two-element orbit \{\lambda,\lambda'\}. So d_{\mathrm{II}} is the indicator of \lambda=\lambda' recoded as \{2,3\}, and the content of the conjecture is the existence of the lift \hat e_\lambda. Under the hypotheses (H-match) and (H-parity) of Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)) item 4, such a realisation forces odd-depth components to vanish on self-conjugate cells and to be antisymmetric on chiral pairs; non-vanishing is the remaining conjectural input.

and the bridge map is given by the action of e_\lambda on the depth-d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) component of \mathrm{Li}_n^q at the canonical Bring shape parameter for cell \lambda.

Structural justification of the statement

The two filtrations have orthogonal information:

  • Iterated-integral depth counts how many polylogarithm factors are needed to express a grouplike — equivalently, the Goncharov motivic-Galois weight.
  • Max-hook depth is a statistic of the partition labelling a cell. It is not the Bruhat length of any element.

They cannot be equal in general (different units; one counts "transcendental complexity," the other counts "algebraic combinatorial complexity"). But they are bridged by the central idempotents, which simultaneously:

  • live in Z(H_n(q)) at a specific max-hook depth, and
  • pair under Markov trace with grouplikes at a specific iterated- integral depth.

The bridge map \lambda \mapsto d_{\mathrm{II}}(\lambda) is what the conjecture predicts.

Concrete predictions

\lambda \mathrm{depth}_{\mathrm{GB}} d_{\mathrm{II}} Period type witnessed
(2,2) self-conj. 3 2 \mathrm{Vol}(4_1) \in \mathcal{P}_2^+
(3), (1,1,1) chiral pair 3 3 \mathrm{CS}(3_1) \in \mathcal{P}_3^-
(2, 1) self-conj. 3 2 hyperbolic vol if 3-mfd (not T(2,3) = 3_1)
(4), (1^4) chiral pair 4 3 (none assigned)
(2, 2, 1, \ldots) depends 2 if self-conj, 3 if pair \ldots

The period column is a comparison: the cell-to-knot assignment is chosen, not derived, and is not part of the conjecture.

The general pattern: self-conjugacy under partition transpose \Rightarrow even iterated-integral depth (real period); chiral pair \Rightarrow odd depth (Tate-twisted period). Verifies Chirality structure on Goncharov period classes via the bar involution.

Reduction to known structure

At n = 2, 3, 4: the table above can be checked exhaustively against the Hecke-cell structure. Self-conjugate partitions of small n are (1), (2,1), (2,2), (3,1,1), (3,2,1), \ldots (these are the partitions equal to their transpose, called self-conjugate). The bridge map gives them depth-2 witnesses; chiral pairs split into depth-3 witnesses.

At n \geq 5: the partition combinatorics gets richer; Hoefsmit seminormal form (Hoefsmit seminormal matrices as R-matrix evaluations in H_n(q)) and the explicit e_\lambda formula (Explicit central primitive idempotents e_\lambda via Jucys–Murphy elements) allow the bridge to be computed cell-by-cell.
